title: Pinholes and Missing Spots in Solid Foil Areas

seo.title: Pinholes and Missing Spots in Solid Foil Areas

content:
Pinholes and missing spots are common when stamping large solid foil areas on paper boxes. A small logo may look perfect, while a wide metallic block can still look uneven.

## Why Solid Areas Are Harder

Large areas require even contact across the whole design. If the paper surface is rough, dusty or uneven, the foil may miss small points. If the machine setting is not balanced, one area may transfer better than another.

## Check the Paper Surface

Rough paper, textured paper and coated paper can all show different coverage. If the missing spots follow the paper texture, the substrate is likely a major factor.

## Check the Foil Grade

Some foils are better for fine lines, while others are better for solid coverage. If your design uses large metallic panels, ask for a solid-area foil grade and test it on the real paper.

## Testing Advice

Add one solid block to every approval sheet. Do not approve a foil only from a small logo. Also check brightness, edge clarity and rub resistance after stamping.

## FAQ

### Why does the logo work but the large area fails?

Large areas need more stable coverage and more even contact.

### Can dust cause pinholes?

Yes. Surface cleanliness can affect transfer quality.
